\begin{example} \end{example}[Hamilton--Ivey estimate] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0225 1. ch13:13.3\group Preserved Curvature Conditions

For a three-dimensional Ricci flow normalized as in the Hamilton--Ivey estimate, if $\lambda _1<0$ is the least curvature-operator eigenvalue, then \[ R(x,t)\geq |\lambda _1|(\log |\lambda _1|+\log (1+t)-3). \] Consequently nonnegative curvature operator is attractive. \end{example}
Proof

\sketch ↗ thm:chow-ii-hamilton-ivey The inequality is the Hamilton–Ivey estimate. A negative eigenvalue in a smooth blow-up limit would make the logarithmic right-hand side, after rescaling, unbounded, contradicting smooth convergence.

□
